A1.justification: Both PDFs describe converting random forests and ReLU networks into Gaussian-kernel generative models. All pages, including both versions' appendices, are readable. Corresponding methods and simulations can be matched despite substantial revisions and renaming.

before.justification: v4 reports original results on five simulation families and a human-confidence study with 126 analyzed participants in Section 5.

after.justification: v5 reports original simulation results and experiments on 46 OpenML-CC18 datasets in Section 6, with dataset-level results in Figures 4–9.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming KDF/KDN to KGF/KGN, v5 replaces mixtures of class-specific kernels with nearest-center kernel selection and weighted class counts. Neural similarity changes from thresholded activation-distance weights to matching activation paths; similarities receive sample-dependent exponents. The density bias changes from a training-likelihood-dependent quantity to b/log(n). These substantially change estimation and inference.

E1.justification: The five simulation families remain, with their definitions moved to Appendix B. v5 adds 46 OpenML-CC18 classification datasets spanning different dimensions and class counts, while removing v4's human-confidence task and participant population.

E2.justification: Random forests and ReLU deep networks remain the algorithmic comparators for the proposed models; v5 extends these comparisons to OpenML. Newly cited calibration methods are not evaluated. v4's removed human study compared humans with RF/DN without directly including KDF/KDN in that comparison.

E3.justification: Reported network width increases from 10 to 1,000 nodes in each of four hidden layers. OOD evaluation changes from fixed square-annulus testing with AUROC/FPR@95 to normalized data and distance-dependent sampling. OpenML adds 1,000 samples per hypersphere and a stated 15-bin adaptive calibration metric, although Figures 5 and 8 label it expected calibration error.

E4.justification: v4's human-versus-machine extrapolation analysis, including posterior estimates along an 82-degree line, is removed. v5 replaces fixed-region OOD confidence analyses varying training size with confidence-versus-distance sweeps, extending these robustness analyses to OpenML in Figures 3, 6 and 9.

E5.justification: v4 Figure 2 explicitly reports 45 repetitions. v5 retains median curves and 25th/75th-percentile bands but omits the repetition count. Its benchmark summary separately identifies variability across 46 datasets. These reporting changes do not establish any increase or decrease in experimental runs.

E6.justification: v4's AUROC/FPR@95 table and human posterior results disappear. v5 adds extensive OpenML results showing OOD-calibration benefits, stronger ID-calibration benefits for KGF than KGN, and classification errors often modestly higher than the parent models. Simulation results are also replaced under revised methods and settings, preventing interpretation as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v4's single asymptotic-unbiasedness argument is replaced by a consistency theorem with hypercube-partition and bandwidth assumptions, supported by bias and variance lemmas in Appendix A. v5 adds an OOD-convergence theorem and a claimed uniform posterior-convergence corollary. The formal ID/OOD setting also changes from disjoint distribution supports to a high-density region and its complement.

C1.justification: v5 drops the abstract's sample-efficiency, small-sample superiority and human-similarity claims, emphasizing density consistency and joint ID/OOD calibration. The conclusion replaces v4's unconditional claim of avoiding any ID-performance sacrifice with accuracy close to the parent models and acknowledgment of possible losses.

C2.justification: Biological-intelligence and lifelong-learning interpretations are removed. v5 explains how nearest-center selection, pruning and Euclidean distance can enlarge polytopes and reduce classification accuracy, particularly on non-Euclidean manifolds. Section 7 proposes geodesic distance and explicitly acknowledges the missing comparisons with other calibration approaches.

D1.justification: v5 Tables 1–2 disclose kernel-weight exponent schedules, bias values and regularization settings; Appendix D adds hardware, operating-system and software-version information. Conversely, v5 omits v4's explicit code-and-experiments repository link. This changes the documented access information without establishing that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v5 introduces a dedicated related-work and contributions section, contrasting discriminative and generative OOD approaches and positioning joint calibration against methods including Ren, Wan and Meinke. It adds calibration, uncertainty-forest and geodesic-forest literature while removing v4's kernel-density OOD, lifelong-learning and OOD-learning references. This substantially revises research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion are extensively rewritten. Methods are reorganized around a common model, desiderata, theory and parameter estimation. Simulation definitions move to Appendix B, proofs expand into Appendix A, and algorithms are consolidated in Appendix C. The title, author information and method terminology also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redesigned into separate forest/network comparison blocks with distance axes. The human-study figure and OOD score table are removed; v5 adds a benchmark summary, six dataset-level figure grids and two hyperparameter tables. Posterior visualizations are redrawn, and algorithm boxes move from duplicated main/appendix displays to the appendices.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens empirical grounding beyond v4's two-dimensional simulations through the 46-dataset benchmark, exposing both calibration benefits and accuracy tradeoffs. Its qualified conclusions and concrete applicability limitations improve claim–evidence alignment, while added implementation details aid assessment. Losing the repetition count and code link weakens reproducibility, and calibration-baseline comparisons remain missing, but broader validation and more candid claims provide a substantial net improvement.
